utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. If I could remind you, sir, of the affirmation you took at the commencement of your evidence which still applies. Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I could ask that Exhibit P54 be placed before the witness. And actually we have a version of it where the names of the -- underneath the photos are blacked out. For the record, that's the one that's going to be placed before the witness. And I would ask that the -- I'm just going to go through these pictures in order, and if the first one could be placed before the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. We are -- I'm going to remind you that we are in open session. Can you understand me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to go through these pictures and ask you each -- with respect to each one if you recognise the person in the photograph. I need to for purposes of the record read out each number that is shown to you. The first one is 0323-1471. Do you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The next one is 0323-1436. Do you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew this person before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know this person's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person is from Godance village. Ahmeti is his last name. This is Vesel Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When is the last time you saw this person, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember when was the last time I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next one U003-8691. Do you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The next one is U008-3669.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It actually -- in there it has a different number, but it is -- it's the same photograph. And if the Court and Defence counsel wish to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Next one is U003-2164. Do you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know this person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person on the photograph in front of me, I recognise him. I have seen him in Lapusnik when I was taken to the second room. This person is Emin Emini, and he was in the second group when Shala divided us into groups. He was in the same group with me and he remained death -- dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next picture, it's U003-8693. Do you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me that this person is Hysri from Belince.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could go to the next one, which is U003-2165.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The next one is U003-8694.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Next one is U003-8695.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know this person either.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The next one is U003-8696.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person whom I've seen in Lapusnik is Shaban Hoti. Then he was not wearing glasses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The next one is U003-8697.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person, I've seen him in Lapusnik and he was on the execution site. And his name is Hasan Hoxha.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The next one is U003-8698.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Safet Hyseni. I've seen him in Lapusnik in the second group on the execution site.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The next one is U003-2166.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know this person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know this person either.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not this one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this person either.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for this person, I heard about him from (redacted). This is a person who I referred to as the traffic policeman from Suhareke area who used to work in Pristina for some time. This is the person who (redacted) referred to. This is a person who had his legs broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The next one is U003-2168.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person is Musli Musliu from Belince who, in short, is called Mus. I've seen him in the first room. I've seen Shala beat him. And on the last day when we left, I have seen this person when I said that as we were leaving the door was open.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The next one is U003-2170.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for this person, I can say that I just know he comes from Xhemtafa family; I don't know his name. Xhemtafa family consists of many members. I don't know his exact name, but I just know that he is a member of this family.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The next one is U003-8702.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person is Bashkim. I don't know his last name. I didn't know at the time whether he lived in Shtime or in the Shtime area. He was in the same room with me. He was in the second group, and he was at the execution site where he was killed. I knew this person before the war as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This person is from Xhemtafa family. I don't know his name, but I know that he is a member of the Xhemtafa family from Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you see this person at Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen this person in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And let me -- if I -- if the usher could go back to U003-2170, please, which is one, two, three, four, five -- oh, it's on page 21. I don't know if that's blocked out also. Witness, you testified that this person is also from the Xhemtafa family, but I didn't ask you: Did you see this person at Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen this person in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back -- the last one I believe we did was 1447. Let's go to U003-8704.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person is Luta, a forest ranger. He worked as a forest ranger at the time, and he comes from Crni Breg village. I knew him from before the war. I saw him at Lapusnik; he was in my room. I saw him -- he was in my group and he was executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The next one is U003-8705.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen this person in Lapusnik. This is Shyq from Godance. This is the person who had his leg broken. This is a person who we carried from Lapusnik to the execution site, and that's where he was killed. I used to know this person before the war, and (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the next group I'm going to ask to go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir, I represent [Realtime transcript read in error: "respect"] Fatmir Limaj, and I want to ask you questions about one particular incident, that is the incident you describe occurring after you had left Lapusnik on the last day and you were on a mountain path when you say Shala mentioned that Commander Celiku was coming and he spoke to Commander Celiku. That's the incident I want to ask you about. Do you understand clearly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, so far I understand you clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that you did not mention or describe this incident nor the name Celiku to anyone in authority until the year 2001 in the summer after you had seen Fatmir Limaj on television?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although the question was quite long, I will answer it. Until 2001, I never mentioned the name of Fatmir Limaj. For the first time I mentioned it in my statement when I came back from the western countries in August 2001. The first time I heard Fatmir Limaj's name was in the mill of Xheladin Ademaj, but I was convinced that I will recognise him as Xhela told me, As soon as you see him on TV, you will recognise him. And before that, I couldn't say to anyone that this is a person from the Lapusnik zone or from some other zone. I know very well that during my first statement, I did not know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Sir, could I just alter one matter in the transcript. It doesn't matter very much. On my first question although "respect" may be appropriate, the word should be "represent." Now, sir, I -- you haven't answered the question I asked. I will ask it again. Do you agree -- I'll split it up. Do you agree that you did not mention or describe any incident on the mountain involving a commander by whatever name, until the year 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. The question was: Do you agree that you did not mention this incident, leave aside names for the moment, you didn't mention the incident or describe it until 2001 in the summer. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before August 2001, I know that I have not mentioned it because before August 2001 at one occasion when I gave a statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You agree, therefore, you did not mention the incident before the summer of 2001. Do you also agree that you did not mention the name "Celiku" to the authorities before the summer of 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the summer of 2001, I did not know the real name of Commander Celiku, but I have mentioned Commander Celiku. But as for his name, I did not know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. Please listen to the question. I ask it again. You did not mention the name -- the name "Celiku," you did not mention that name to anyone in authority until the summer of 2001, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And I'm going to suggest to you that you only mentioned the name Celiku and this incident on the mountain after you saw Fatmir Limaj on television. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And I want to ask you clearly if you saw Commander -- a man called Commander Celiku on the mountain on your last day before those terrible events you have described, how was it that you did not mention a Commander Celiku to anyone in authority before the summer of 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will now explain this issue, and you will understand why I did not mention him. First of all, when the killing occurred I was in a very terrible state. Something that I never imagined happened. Secondly, we Albanians from Kosovo, we have the blood feud. As I have seen with my own eyes the killing of (redacted) my friends, at that moment I forgot not only Commander Celiku but I also forgot Qerqiz; I was just oriented at Shala and Murrizi and the person who directly participated in the killing. I did not even think at that time that things will go step by step. As I left Lapusnik, how the journey proceeded, what happened, this is all that I said later. I said that Murrizi and Shala left with us from Lapusnik, and then I mentioned that on the middle of the journey someone assigned a soldier to us and that this was Commander Celiku. And this is how it was brought up. And before that, I wasn't thinking of this. It was the first time that I saw a killing with my eyes. So I was orientated at Shala, not at the other two; so this is the reason. With investigators we worked the whole event step by step, from my house, to Lapusnik, to the prison, to the journey to the execution site, the killing itself. So this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You say you focused on Shala. You say this person who mentioned Commander Celiku was Shala, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was Shala that said, Commander Celiku is coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: If you're focusing on Shala --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: If you're focusing on Shala after these events, how could you forget that perhaps the most important officer in the region or zone, according to you, had been present three hours before the execution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will explain it like this, and this is how it was. This was a person, as you call him, the high-ranking officer, but it is a fact that he personally did not torture him -- me, (redacted) at the cherry tree. 17 He did not say that this commander tortured him or maltreated him. (redacted) (redacted) just told me about things that befell on him and that were caused by Shala and by Qerqizi. So I was focused on Shala and Qerqizi. (redacted) (redacted) even said that Murrizi did not cause him any trouble during the time in prison. So this is mainly the reason why. At that time, I was just looking for Shala to find out his identity, to find out the identity of the person who's killing persons without any reason. Even -- if it wasn't for this trial today -- if it wasn't for this trial today, I would never ask who Fatmir Limaj was, but the investigation asked, Who was that person? What happened? How it happened. So this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I will come to the investigation by the CCIU, but first you spoke to Serbian police authorities in some detail, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And I want to examine that opportunity you had to mention Celiku if you had seen him, and I want to make it clear on Fatmir Limaj's behalf that there was no such incident on the mountain where he arrived on a tractor or walking. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I follow very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to take this part carefully. After the shocking executions, you were clearly extremely frightened and extremely worried, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And your main worry was that perhaps somebody from the KLA might pursue you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Could we have on screen, please, map 6 of P1. May I ask if it's on screen --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Sorry. Could the map be on screen so we can all see it as well, please? No. Well, can I proceed on the basis everyone has the map, even if it's not on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Could you kindly look at this map -- have you seen this particular map before? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: If you look at it, you will see that Lapusnik is marked inside a red square, and if you come below the square you will see a red triangle which marks roughly Berisa. Do you see those two places, Lapusnik and Berisa, on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see Lapusnik and Berisa in the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, some other places on this map. If you go to the bottom, right-hand corner, you will see Ferizaj marked with a red dot and a pink area around it. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, the first thing I want to ask you is whether you're telling the truth about the fact that you -- having left the area of the executions, that you went on foot all the way from the Berisa mountains to Ferizaj. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. From this place I went to Ferizaj to a (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you go by road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I did not go by road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Because to go over the mountains, it's a very considerable distance, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not go on the mountains. I went from Berisa to Baijice, to Nekovce. (redacted) lives in Nekovce, but I did not dare go to her. In Sedlare, (redacted) I was afraid that Shala could find me because (redacted). So I did not know where to go. That's why I went to a (redacted). (redacted), and I arrived there the next day at 6.00 p.m., around that time. She still lives there in the same house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: On this map, just indicate, would you, the route that you took.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From Berisa, I went to Nekovce. I went this way. This the Lipovica wire which goes to Krajiste. I did not stay in Lipovica because it was under KLA control. I went to Zborce and I did not stay there because I was afraid that it was under their control. I went here to Godance. Godance as well was under KLA controls, so I was avoiding the area. I went to the main road here from Shtime to Lipjan, crossed it. I went here to Muzeqine, which is an area I know very well, Koshare e Teli [as interpreted] and here, before getting to (redacted), I knew that I could stay for a week or so in this area and then leave. It was around 5.00 or 6.00 p.m. when I arrived there. (redacted) (redacted). That's where I had a fresh set of clothes. I shaved. (redacted) (redacted) started giving me a massage because I was in a very bad shape. She knew what had happened to (redacted), but she did not know about the killing. The SUP is only 700 metres away from her house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, the question I have is this: That distance across the mountains is going to be, looking at the scale on this map, somewhere between 40 and 50 kilometres; by road, it's 39 direct, roughly. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, approximately. Possibly 35 or 40 kilometres, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. Across the mountains it's over 40, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you avoid all checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no checkpoints in these -- in this area of Drenica. On the at the crossroad in Gjurkoc. I passed through this area because I know this area very well, and I ended up in Ferizaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And are you saying you risked being caught by the KLA by going through territory occupied by them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not go close to the houses or the villages, but still the danger was great. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I suggest you did no such thing. Instead, looking at the map, what I suggest you did was that you could see the Serb checkpoint from the mountains near Berisa. You could see the checkpoint Komorane, which is to the north and to the right of Lapusnik on this map. Do you see Komorane?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see Komorane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You could see that checkpoint from the mountains where you had been, couldn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the execution, I couldn't see anything. After it became dark, I began to move. I did not dare to move before that. But I did not know where exactly the Komorane checkpoint was, and I did not see any lights there. And I didn't even know that there was a checkpoint there. I learned about that checkpoint when I was taken there, when I went to Pristina and was taken to Komorane. But when it was becoming dark -- before becoming dark, I did not dare to move. But as I said, I know this area very well and I walked all the area on foot all the time. The Serbs took me from Pristina to Komorane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You knew at this time that Komorane was a Serb checkpoint, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I did not know what kind of forces were in Komorane or what was there in Komorane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You knew it was a --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You knew it was a Serb checkpoint. It was the biggest in Kosovo at that time, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not know until the moment I was taken there, I did not know that there was a checkpoint there or whether there were any forces there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What I suggest you did when it was light, not during the night, you went down to the checkpoint and handed yourself over to Serb police, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And just following the map, you then went with Serb police to Pristina, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I went from Ferizaj to Pristina with the Serbian police. It's the opposite way, not the way you describe it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And just to finish this part of what I suggest is having got to Pristina you made a statement in Pristina and then were taken down to SUP in Ferizaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I want you to look at a statement, or rather a report made by the Serb authorities about a visit that you made in Ferizaj and also in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, the -- there is a bundle available to everybody, and it is in fact within that bundle, the second statement. And we have it in English and in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: A particular page -- I can give the number for the English version as well I want you to look at -- the ERN number is 0306-6563. And for the Albanian it will be 0308-3263. Now, sir, if you as a witness would look at the Albanian version which you can read, 0308-3263, I'll put the question in English, which will be translated so that you can find it in the Albanian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, on our page it's 0306-6563. It's halfway down this page beginning with the English words "further in his account."

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your name is there, then -- I don't read it out obviously -- "Stated that running through the forest from the direction of Lapusnik, he came to the Pristina-Pec main road and he gave himself up to a policeman at a checkpoint in Komorane and recounted the incident to them, after which he was taken over by officials of the DB State Security Service in Pristina, who conducted a detailed interview with him. "After conducting the interview with," you, and your name is mentioned again, "in the premises of the Urosevac SUP, on orders from the chief of the Urosevac SUP OSL, authorised officials of the Urosevac SUP OKP crime investigation department, together with," you, and so on, "went to the village of Lapusnik." I've just summarised. That was said at the beginning of August by you to those Serb authorities, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this statement, but I don't know that I've given this in Pristina. I know that from Ferizaj we went to Pristina. In Pristina we waited for an hour, an hour and a half and another car joined us. I can see the names here and these are correct, all of them, and these names I've given in Ferizaj. Pristina was also aware about the case, what had happened, because we went from Ferizaj to Pristina. I was waiting in the car. We waited for some time. The inspector went inside; I don't know what they were talking about in there. So we left for Komorane, and from there to Lapusnik. And all the names here, Bashkim, Xheladin Ademaj, all the names are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I suggest you are avoiding the point. The point you are making to the Serbian authorities is that you went to a Serb police checkpoint, which you've said this afternoon you didn't know existed, in Komorane and recounted the incident to them, and then after that Pristina. How did the Serb authorities -- this is the question: How did the Serb authorities manage to get that version down if it did not happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian authorities have taken the statement from me; it is true. I can see all the names here, and the names were mentioned by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So you did hand yourself in, didn't you, to the Serb authorities, and before today, you have been anxious not to admit that. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not like that. I was taken in Ferizaj. My first interview was in Ferizaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So why does this report not indicate anything about being stopped at a checkpoint in Ferizaj because you had no documents and so forth? There's no mention of it in this statement or report, to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've given two statements to the Serbs. The first statement when I was stopped by the police, I was together with a relative, and the second one when I went to -- when I was at the police station. And it is true that I was stopped at Ferizaj. So that is true that I was stopped by the Ferizaj police and taken to the SUP, and it was the same inspector for the second time -- for the first time and the second time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'll come to the inspector in a minute. The fact is this report, covering the time from when you left the execution site makes no mention of you being stopped in Ferizaj because you had no documents. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Can you explain therefore why they don't have any record of you being stopped in Ferizaj as opposed to giving yourself up to the Serb police at Komorane and being taken to Pristina and then down to Ferizaj? How is the account so different?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Serb statements always had differences. It was a wartime at the time. I don't know what they wrote in there, but I know that these names given here were given by me. And it is true that I went from Ferizaj to Pristina in a car. We were four people. I waited there for an hour and a half when they went inside there. I don't know when they wrote this. I can't tell you when they wrote this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: They wrote the report, if you look at 030 -- and in your case it will be 0308-3261. In the English version it's 0306-6561. You will see that at the top of the report it mentions that it's dated the 5th of August, 1998. And in the first paragraph it suggests that you came of your own accord and reported the following. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You did go of your own accord to the Serb authorities, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So that's wrong as well, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What the Serbian authorities did here, I don't know -- well, I couldn't go. There was no way I could go to the Serbian forces at midnight, and I didn't even know that there were Serbian forces there. Because I have told them the truth when they asked me the first time, Are there any KLA in Petrove? I said, No. They asked me, Who are the people in uniform? And I said, I don't know. The second time when they asked me in Ferizaj I told them where I had been, but they did not believe me. And that's why they took me to find the place, to verify the story from Ferizaj to Pristina. I waited for two hours in the car. They went inside, discussed things, I don't know. And then we went to Komorane, and then I saw that there was so many forces in Komorane there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Could you just concentrate on the questions, and it may be a little bit quicker, please. Thank you. I'm going to suggest to you that the reason the report suggests you gave yourself up at a checkpoint near Komorane is of course you knew Serb -- or (redacted) knew Serb police officers quite well, didn't you? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbian policemen in Komorane?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. You tell us where the Serbian police officers were that you knew quite well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbian officer with the exception of the commander in (redacted), that everybody knew him. I did not know any other Serbian officers. Maybe an odd policeman here and there that everybody knew in (redacted). I'm not sure what you're talking about, sir. (redacted) was not involved in the army or the SUP; he was just a civilian. 70 per cent of my time was spent outside the country and 30 per cent in my country. And there I went on hunting parties. I don't know where you got this, and we did not know any Serbian officers. We were never part of the authorities or any structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you know what the -- some Serbian police officers have said about (redacted) and their knowledge of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]

utterances.text: And he says that he -- to the authorities investigating this case, that he knew (redacted) personally. They were friendly people who didn't oppose the Serb authorities. I often stopped by (redacted) for a drink, and I went hunting with them. I've left the names out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is wrong, that -- this person Momcilo Sparavalo has never been to (redacted). He did not come with us on hunting parties. He never had a gun to go on hunting parties. There was another person, (redacted), that person, who was a manager of a hotel, he was interested in hunting. This person never was interested in hunting, and I never spoke to him or had a conversation with him before the day I was there in Jasovic's office. And there I did not speak to him either. He just came in, went out, came in, went out, all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Can you think of a reason why this police officer should therefore lie about his relationship with (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying the truth now. It's the same surname, but the name is different. It's (redacted) and he knew (redacted), and he went to hunting parties with (redacted) and he has been to (redacted). But not the person you are saying here. And I'm saying this and it's the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Dragan Jasovic, the other officer, also says that he was invited in for a drink at your (redacted). Do you deny that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say I deny it or I admit it. It could have happened, but I have not (redacted). I have been abroad most of the time. But when I personally was (redacted), he has never been to (redacted) while I was there. I know that once (redacted) had a pistol that he did not have a legal permit to keep, and Dragan Jasovic had come to the -- to (redacted) to take that pistol away. And in fact, (redacted) (redacted). And you can verify that, that sentence. And you can verify as well whether Dragan Jasovic was there to drink something or to take the pistol away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm just putting to you what he describes of being invited in for a drink, not to recover a gun. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So again, why would he be lying about his relationship with (redacted) (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-96 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you mentioned somebody else who went on hunting with (redacted), I can say that they -- these persons went hunting with (redacted), but not Dragan Jasovic.
